tool_analysis:
Step Analysis:
- The recorded browser session navigated to Magento Admin > Online Customers, closed an overlay, filled multiple filter inputs (ID, First Name, Email, Last URL, Type) and applied Search. The IP filter input was not reliably detected in the DOM (JS-disabled banner observed), so URL-based filter application was attempted.

Task Definition:
- Create a deterministic, reusable tool that applies the requested Online Customers filters (ID, name/email, IP, last URL, Type, Last Activity date range) and returns the resulting grid contents. The tool should prefer URL-based filter application (reliable in non-JS environments) and use a small set of stable UI actions (overlay close, Search click) to support JS-enabled grids.

Action Plan:
1) Navigate to the provided admin_base_url (Online Customers page).
2) Close the recorded overlay (elementHash df76c6ce85) to ensure filters are accessible.
3) Construct and navigate to a URL that includes the filter query parameters (filter[...] mapping). This is the deterministic PASS 2 optimization: one navigation applies the filters server-side when JS is disabled or the grid supports GET-based filters.
4) If JavaScript is enabled, click the grid Search button (scoped XPath) to ensure client-side filter application and trigger grid refresh.
5) Extract the grid contents and applied filter summary for verification.

Variable Identification (inputs):
- admin_base_url (required): Starting page for the grid.
- filter_id_from, filter_id_to: numeric ID range (optional).
- filter_firstname, filter_middlename, filter_lastname: name filters (optional).
- filter_email: email filter (optional).
- filter_remote_addr: IP filter (optional). Matches filter[remote_addr] param.
- filter_session_start_from, filter_session_start_to: session start date range (optional).
- filter_last_activity_from, filter_last_activity_to: last activity date range (optional).
- filter_type: Type filter (Customer/Visitor) (optional).
- filter_last_url: Last URL filter (optional).
- form_key: optional token if caller prefers including it.

Step Optimization:
- Prefer URL-based filter application (single navigation with query parameters) because it's deterministic and avoids fragile UI selectors and timing issues.
- Use a recorded overlay-close elementHash to deterministically dismiss the popup that previously blocked access.
- After navigation with filters, still perform a scoped Search button click to accommodate JS-enabled grids that require an explicit client-side trigger.
- The tool intentionally includes both server-side URL application and client-side click to be resilient across environments (JS enabled/disabled).

Selector Decisions & Robustness:
- Anchor selectors to the 'Online Customers' heading and the grid table where possible (XPath used in the Search click). For overlay close we use the recorded elementHash (stable for the recorded session) as the fastest deterministic target.
- The tool builds query parameters using the exact 'filter[...]' naming convention seen in the session (e.g. filter[remote_addr]) so developers can map inputs directly to server-side filter names.

Edge cases & notes for implementers:
- If storage_state errors were previously observed (e.g. invalid storage_state file), ensure the automation checks for a valid storage_state file before creating a browser context; if missing/corrupt, perform a standard login and save a fresh storage state (not part of this tool which assumes a valid session).
- If the IP input is not present in the DOM (JS-disabled or custom admin theme), the URL-based approach is the recommended fallback (filter%5Bremote_addr%5D=IP). If the backend uses LIKE for matching, attempt '%IP%' wildcard values.

This tool is single-purpose and deterministic: build the filter URL from inputs, navigate, click Search for client-side triggers, and return grid results.
name: magento_admin_online_customers_filter_tool
description: Apply filters to the Magento Admin 'Online Customers' grid (customer_online) and extract the resulting grid. Uses URL-based filter application (deterministic) and a small set of stable UI actions (close overlay, click Search) as a compatibility step. Assumes valid admin session (tool does not perform authentication).

steps.description: Navigate to the Online Customers admin page (anchor to the grid).
Short wait for page to load and for any overlays or grid to render.
Close the 'Incoming Message' overlay if present (recorded close link). This uses the recorded elementHash to deterministically target the overlay close control.
Allow overlay to dismiss and DOM to settle.

Navigate to the same admin page with URL-encoded filter parameters to apply filters server-side. This is deterministic and avoids fragile UI interactions when possible. Empty parameters are included but the server will ignore them.
Wait for the server to respond and the grid to render with applied filters (server-side fallback for JS-disabled environments).
Click the grid 'Search' button in the filter row to trigger client-side filtering if JavaScript is enabled (scoped to the Online Customers grid).
Wait for client-side grid refresh (AJAX or page reload) after Search click.
Capture the filtered grid contents and applied filter values so the caller can verify results.
steps.goal: Extract applied filter summary, grid column headers, rows, total records found, and visible 'No records found' message.

input_schema.name: admin_base_url
input_schema.description: Full admin page URL for the Online Customers grid, e.g. 'http://dockerized-magento.local/index.php/admin/customer_online/'. Must include protocol and host.

input_schema.name: filter_id_from
input_schema.description: ID filter - 'From' value (numeric). Maps to filter[id][from] when present.

input_schema.name: filter_id_to
input_schema.description: ID filter - 'To' value (numeric). Maps to filter[id][to] when present.

input_schema.name: filter_firstname
input_schema.description: First name filter value. Maps to filter[firstname] when present.

input_schema.name: filter_middlename
input_schema.description: Middle name filter value. Maps to filter[middlename] when present.

input_schema.name: filter_lastname
input_schema.description: Last name filter value. Maps to filter[lastname] when present.

input_schema.name: filter_email
input_schema.description: Email filter value. Maps to filter[email] when present.

input_schema.name: filter_remote_addr
input_schema.description: IP Address filter value. Maps to filter[remote_addr] (or filter[ip]) when present. Use dotted IPv4 (e.g. '203.0.113.45').

input_schema.name: filter_session_start_from
input_schema.description: Session Start Time 'From' value (YYYY-MM-DD or site-expected format). Maps to filter[session_start][from].

input_schema.name: filter_session_start_to
input_schema.description: Session Start Time 'To' value (YYYY-MM-DD or site-expected format). Maps to filter[session_start][to].

input_schema.name: filter_last_activity_from
input_schema.description: Last Activity 'From' date (YYYY-MM-DD). Maps to filter[last_activity][from].

input_schema.name: filter_last_activity_to
input_schema.description: Last Activity 'To' date (YYYY-MM-DD). Maps to filter[last_activity][to].

input_schema.name: filter_type
input_schema.description: Type filter (Customer/Visitor). Provide the option value used by the site (e.g. 'c' or 'customer'). If unknown, provide visible text (the tool will place it into query).

input_schema.name: filter_last_url
input_schema.description: Last URL (path) filter value (e.g. '/checkout/cart'). Maps to filter[last_url].

input_schema.name: form_key
input_schema.description: Optional admin form_key token. If known, include it; otherwise tool will attempt URL-based filter without it.
